'''David Egorovich Dolidze''' ({{lang-ka|დავით დოლიძე}}, {{langx|ru|Давид Егорович Долидзе}}) ({{OldStyleDate|2 February|1908|20 January}} – 1960) was a [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] and [[Soviet]] [[mathematician]],<ref name="Kurosh_p237">See {{harv|Kurosh|Vityushkov|Boltyanskii|Dynkin|1959|p=237}}.</ref> known from his work in the mathematical theory of [[fluid motion]]. In particular he rediscovered an important uniqueness theorem for the [[classical solution]]s to the Navier–Stokes equations for an [[incompressible fluid]], previously proved by [[Emanuele Foà]].<ref>See {{harv|Serrin|1959|loc=p. 251, footnote 1}} and {{harv|Serrin|1959b|p=271}}.</ref>

==Life and academic career==
Born on 2 February 1908 in the [[village]] of Buknari,<ref>{{harvtxt|Kurosh|Vityushkov|Boltyanskii|Dynkin|1959|p=237}} precisely use the locution "''с.  Букнари''", i.e. село Букнари ({{lang-ka|ბუკნარი}}).</ref> He graduated from Tbilisi State University in 1928.<ref name="Kurosh_p237" /> From 1934 he started working in his [[Alma Mater]], and one year later, in 1935, he also started doing research at the Mathematics Institute of the [[Georgian Academy of Science]].<ref name="Kurosh_p237" /> In 1945 he earned both the [[Doktor Nauk]] degree and the title of [[professor]].<ref name="Kurosh_p237" />

The "''Mathematics in the [[USSR]] during its first forty years 1917–1957''" is an opus in two volumes describing the developments of Soviet mathematics during the first forty years of its existence. This is the second volume, titled "''Biobibliography''" (evidently an [[acronym]] for [[biography]] and [[bibliography]]), containing a complete bibliography of works published by Soviet mathematicians during that time period, alphabetically ordered with respect to author's surname and including, when possible, brief but complete biographies of the authors.
